title: Aerial Object Tracking
summary: C++ and OpenCV prototypes exploring the detection and tracking of selected objects in aerial imagery.
problem: Aerial imagery can support more autonomous sensing when relevant objects can be identified and tracked over time.
approach: Explored detection and tracking of moving and selected stationary objects.
Used C++ and OpenCV to process aerial-video imagery.
Contributed to invention documentation connecting visual information with a UAV-control concept.
outcome: Computer-vision prototypes and concept documentation forming a foundation for further embedded-vision research.

sections.title: Detection and tracking in aerial imagery
body: C++/OpenCV prototypes explore moving objects and selected stationary objects in aerial video, connecting computer vision with autonomous sensing.

sections.title: Visual information for more autonomous decisions
body: The project concept considers how extracted visual information could support onboard UAV decisions and reduce dependence on a human operator and continuous ground communication.

sections.title: A collaborative concept
body: The invention documentation names Hossein Niromandi and Sina Shiri. The work combines image processing, electronics and machine vision in an aerial-sensing context.

strength: A study of detection and tracking over time.
result: Computer-vision prototypes and concept documentation forming a foundation for further embedded-vision research.
decisionNotes: The C++/OpenCV desktop prototypes process recorded aerial and road footage, with operator selection, region detection and adjustable area, threshold and morphology controls. The separate collaborative concept connects extracted visual information with possible onboard UAV decisions.
validationNotes: Six archival desktop recordings show vehicle-region detection, selected-target tracking and adjustable image-processing controls over recorded footage. The cover is a labelled AI concept illustration. These artifacts demonstrate desktop prototypes; they do not establish an onboard UAV implementation, flight validation or measured tracking accuracy.
